status_summary: Around 2025-10-29 the President publicly said the United States would begin testing nuclear weapons on an equal basis with other countries; on 2025-11-02 the Energy Secretary said the tests would be non-explosive systems tests. CRS (2025-12-16) reported it was unclear what policy change would follow, that the standing goal is readiness to test within 24 to 36 months of a presidential decision, and that the United States has not ratified the test ban treaty. On 2026-05-13 the Energy Secretary told senators explosive testing is not needed for reliability, and an NNSA experiment announced 2026-10-01 was non-nuclear. The sources reviewed show no order moving NNSA to immediate test readiness.

timeline.event: The President posted that, because other countries test, he had instructed the Department of War to begin testing US nuclear weapons on an equal basis, starting immediately (dated from an AIP report that places the post on the prior Wednesday); no written order was identified.
The Energy Secretary said the planned tests would be systems tests of weapon components and not nuclear explosions.
At a Senate hearing the Energy Secretary said a testing decision rests with the President and that explosive testing is not needed to assure weapon reliability, per a senator's release.
NNSA announced a subsurface non-nuclear chemical high-explosive experiment at the Nevada site to improve detection of low-yield nuclear explosions; it was not a nuclear test.

title: Direct NNSA to nuclear test readiness and signal willingness to test
uncertainties: The President's social media post was not retrieved; its date (about 2025-10-29) is inferred from press accounts, and an AIP report quotes it as an instruction to the Department of War. The CRS report of 2025-12-16 was read in full and identifies no executive order or other binding directive resulting from the statements; it links a Reuters report of 2025-10-30 whose text was not read. A Federal Register query on 2026-10-17 for the term nuclear weapons testing since 2025-10-01 returned no documents, which does not rule out a non-published directive. The readiness element overlaps the existing DoD-chapter record c04-06, which tracks restoring test readiness; this record also covers the treaty and signaling elements. Related bills, read on govinfo.gov bill status records on 2026-10-22: H.R. 5894 (the RESTRAIN Act, introduced 2025-10-31, 29 cosponsors, latest action sponsor remarks on 2025-11-19) would amend the Atomic Energy Defense Act to prohibit explosive nuclear testing by the United States, and S. 3090 (introduced 2025-10-30, 8 cosponsors) would bar the use of funds for an explosive nuclear weapons test; H.R. 5951 (introduced 2025-11-07, 3 cosponsors) and the identical S. 3106 (introduced 2025-11-05, 5 cosponsors) would require congressional approval before explosive testing resumes. All four were referred to committee, and none has had committee action or been enacted. These bills run opposite to the recommended willingness to test, so they are treated as related context and not as steps toward it; because none is law, they do not support a diverged stage. An external retrieval of 2026-10-22 searched Congress.gov and agency sources for a directive to NNSA, a budget action or a defense authorization provision shortening test readiness and found none; its description of a 24 to 36 month readiness posture matches the existing CRS source, but its agency items carried no links and were not re-opened, and its further funding details are not relied on. The FY2026 and FY2027 defense authorization texts were not read in full, so a readiness provision cannot be ruled out. Independent review of 2026-10-16: the CRS report of 2025-12-16 (no formal order identified, readiness goal 24 to 36 months, treaty signed but not ratified) and the Nevada delegation letter of 2025-11-03 asking that the directive be withdrawn were moved here from the timeline, as an analysis and a members' letter rather than government actions; both remain cited sources.
